node.title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants: Pre-fertilisation: structure and events – stamen,

questions.stem: The stalk that attaches an ovule to the placenta of the ovary is called the
questions.explanation: The ovule is attached to the placenta by a stalk called the funicle. The point where the funicle joins the body of the ovule is the hilum, while the basal end opposite the micropyle is the chalaza. The funicle is therefore the stalk itself.

optionRationale.1: The hilum is the junction between the funicle and the body of the ovule, not the stalk.
optionRationale.2: The chalaza is the basal part of the ovule where nucellus, integuments and funicle meet.
optionRationale.4: The micropyle is the small opening left by the integuments at the tip of the ovule.

questions.objective: Identify the funicle of an ovule

questions.stem: Which of the following plants is pollinated by wind?
questions.explanation: Maize is a grass and shows wind pollination, with light non-sticky pollen, exposed stamens and feathery stigmas packed in the cob. Hydrilla and Vallisneria are pollinated by water, while the water hyacinth, though aquatic, is pollinated by insects or wind.

optionRationale.1: Hydrilla is a water-pollinated submerged plant.
optionRationale.3: Vallisneria shows hydrophily; its pollen floats on the water surface to the female flower.
optionRationale.4: The water hyacinth is aquatic but is pollinated by insects or wind, not by wind alone in the sense of a grass.

questions.stem: The small opening left at the tip of an ovule by the integuments is the
questions.explanation: The integuments enclose the nucellus but leave a small opening at the tip called the micropyle. The pollen tube usually enters the ovule through it, and in the seed it remains as a pore that helps water and oxygen to enter during germination.

optionRationale.2: The hilum is where the funicle meets the ovule body.
optionRationale.3: The chalaza is at the end opposite to the micropyle.
optionRationale.4: The funicle is the stalk of the ovule, not an opening.

questions.stem: In artificial hybridisation, the term emasculation means
options: covering the flower with a butter-paper bag
dusting the desired pollen on the stigma
removing the stigma from the flower bud
removing the anthers from the bud before they dehisce
questions.explanation: Emasculation is the removal of the anthers from the bud of the female parent before the anthers dehisce, so that self-pollen cannot reach the stigma. After this the flower is bagged and later dusted with the desired pollen.

optionRationale.1: Covering the flower with a bag is bagging, which prevents contamination by unwanted pollen.
optionRationale.2: Dusting the chosen pollen is the pollination step done after emasculation and bagging.
optionRationale.3: The stigma must stay, since it receives the desired pollen; only the anthers are removed.

questions.stem: The filiform apparatus, a special thickening that guides the pollen tube into the embryo sac, is found in the
questions.explanation: The two synergids at the micropylar end of the embryo sac have special cellular thickenings called the filiform apparatus. It guides the pollen tube into the synergid, where the two male gametes are discharged before they reach the egg and the central cell.

optionRationale.1: Antipodals lie at the chalazal end and take no part in guiding the pollen tube.
optionRationale.3: The egg cell is the female gamete; the guiding thickenings are on the synergids beside it.
optionRationale.4: The central cell holds the two polar nuclei and has no filiform apparatus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a typical insect-pollinated flower?
options: Sticky pollen grains that cling to insects
questions.explanation: Insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar, and their pollen is generally sticky so that it clings to the visiting animal. Light, non-sticky pollen is an adaptation of wind-pollinated flowers, which let the air carry the pollen.

optionRationale.1: Showy petals attract insects, so this is a genuine feature.
optionRationale.2: Fragrance and nectar are the rewards that attract insects.
optionRationale.3: Sticky pollen is typical of insect pollination.

questions.objective: Separate adaptations of insect and wind pollination

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about seeds and fruits.
A. The outer testa and inner tegmen of a seed are formed from the integuments.
B. Castor seeds are endospermic.
C. Pea seeds are non-endospermic.
D. Apple is a true fruit because it develops only from the ovary.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The integuments harden into the testa and tegmen, castor keeps its endosperm and pea uses it up before maturity, so A, B and C are correct. Apple is a false fruit because the thalamus also contributes to it, so statement D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Statement C is also correct, so leaving it out is incomplete.
optionRationale.2: Statement A is also correct, so this is incomplete.
optionRationale.4: Statement D is false; the thalamus contributes to apple, making it a false fruit.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on seed coats, endosperm and fruit types

questions.stem: Match List-I (structure) with List-II (feature or role) and choose the correct code.

right: I. Becomes the seed coat after fertilisation
II. The single cotyledon of a grass embryo
III. Innermost wall layer that nourishes developing pollen
IV. Inner wall of the pollen grain made of cellulose and pectin

questions.explanation: The tapetum is the innermost wall layer of the microsporangium and nourishes the pollen (A-III). The intine is the thin inner pollen wall of cellulose and pectin (B-IV). The integuments become the seed coats (C-I). The scutellum is the single cotyledon of a grass embryo (D-II).

optionRationale.2: A and B are interchanged; the tapetum is a wall layer of the anther, not the pollen wall.
optionRationale.3: C and D are interchanged; the scutellum is the cotyledon, and the integuments form the seed coat.
optionRationale.4: A, B and C are wrongly matched; the tapetum does not form a seed coat.

questions.objective: Match reproductive structures with their roles

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): In the water lily and the water hyacinth, pollination is mostly by insects or wind and not by water.
Reason (R): Hydrophily is rare among flowering plants and is found in only about 30 genera, mostly monocots.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. The flowers of the water lily and water hyacinth rise above the water and are pollinated by insects or wind. Hydrophily is rare, but the rarity of water pollination is a general fact and does not by itself explain why these two plants use other agents.

optionRationale.1: R states how uncommon hydrophily is overall, which does not explain the pollination mode of these two particular plants.
optionRationale.3: R is true; about 30 genera, mostly monocots, show water pollination.
optionRationale.4: A is true; these aquatic plants are insect or wind pollinated.

questions.objective: Distinguish aquatic habit from water pollination

questions.stem: Pollen grains of wheat and rice lose their viability within about
questions.explanation: In cereals such as wheat and rice the pollen remains viable for only about 30 minutes after release. In members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae it can remain viable for months. Pollen can also be stored for years in liquid nitrogen at minus 196 degrees Celsius.

optionRationale.1: A month is far longer than the viability of cereal pollen.
optionRationale.2: Months of viability are seen in Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae, not in wheat or rice.
optionRationale.4: Thirty hours is too long; cereal pollen dies within minutes.

questions.stem: A botanist wants 100 functional embryo sacs (monosporic development) and 100 pollen grains. The minimum number of mother cells that must undergo meiosis is
questions.explanation: Each megaspore mother cell gives one functional megaspore and so one embryo sac, so 100 megaspore mother cells are needed. Each pollen mother cell gives four microspores and so four pollen grains, so 100 pollen grains need only 25 pollen mother cells. The total is 100 + 25 = 125.

optionRationale.1: This treats each pollen grain as needing its own mother cell, giving 100 + 100.
optionRationale.2: This adds 100 embryo sac mother cells to 125, which has no basis; pollen needs only 25 mother cells.
optionRationale.3: This counts only the megaspore mother cells and forgets the pollen mother cells.

questions.objective: Calculate mother cells needed for gametophytes

questions.stem: In a mature typical embryo sac, how many nuclei take no part in forming either the zygote or the primary endosperm nucleus?
questions.explanation: The embryo sac has eight nuclei. One is in the egg, which forms the zygote, and two are polar nuclei, which form the primary endosperm nucleus. The remaining 8 - 3 = 5 nuclei belong to the two synergids and the three antipodal cells and do not enter either fusion.

optionRationale.2: Three is the number of nuclei that do take part (one egg and two polar nuclei), or the number of antipodals alone.
optionRationale.3: Six counts the egg apparatus and antipodals but wrongly includes the egg, which does fuse.
optionRationale.4: Four would leave out one of the five non-participating nuclei.

questions.objective: Count non-participating nuclei of the embryo sac

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements.
A. Banana is a parthenocarpic fruit.
B. Parthenocarpy can be induced by the application of auxins.
C. Apomictic seeds are formed only after syngamy between egg and male gamete.
D. In Citrus, embryos formed from nucellar cells are genetically identical to the parent plant.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Banana forms fruit without fertilisation, and auxins can induce this, so A and B are correct. Nucellar embryos of Citrus arise from diploid somatic nucellar cells and are clones of the parent, so D is correct. Apomixis forms seeds without fertilisation, so C is false.

optionRationale.1: Statement D is also correct, so this is incomplete.
optionRationale.3: Statement C is false, since apomixis means seed formation without fertilisation.
optionRationale.4: Statement C is false, and B is correct but left out.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on parthenocarpy and apomixis

questions.stem:
Arrange the following events in the correct sequence.
1. Release of two male gametes into the synergid
2. Germination of pollen on the stigma
3. Entry of the pollen tube into a synergid through the filiform apparatus
4. Syngamy and triple fusion
5. Growth of the pollen tube through the style to the ovule
questions.explanation: The pollen first germinates on the stigma, then the tube grows through the style to the ovule. It enters a synergid through the filiform apparatus, which is where the two male gametes are discharged, and only then do syngamy and triple fusion occur. The order is 2, 5, 3, 1, 4.

optionRationale.1: The tube cannot enter a synergid before it has grown through the style.
optionRationale.2: Growth of the tube cannot precede germination of the pollen.
optionRationale.4: Gametes cannot be released into the synergid before the tube has entered it.

questions.objective: Sequence the events from pollination to fertilisation

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Cleistogamous flowers such as those of Commelina set seeds even when no pollinators are present.
Reason (R): The anthers and stigma of a cleistogamous flower lie close together and the flower never opens, so autogamy is assured.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: In cleistogamous flowers the closed flower keeps the anthers and the stigma next to each other, so pollen reaches the stigma of the same flower without any external agent. This autogamy is exactly why seeds are set without pollinators, so R explains A.

optionRationale.2: R is not just an unrelated fact; the closed flower and close anthers directly cause assured seed set.
optionRationale.3: R is true; cleistogamous flowers never open and have close anthers and stigma.
optionRationale.4: A is true; assured self-pollination gives seeds without pollinators.

questions.objective: Explain assured seed set in cleistogamous flowers
